messages:
mira: Day 4 async check-in — quick status. What I did: finished local runtime build, ran unit tests, created PR for infra doc updates (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/345). Got access to the console, can see projects.
sam: Congrats on the PR! Quick heads-up: CI flaked on lint, might be precommit hook. Did you run `yarn lint` locally?
mira: I did but saw this error on `yarn install` — node-gyp failing: `gyp ERR! stack Error: Can't find Python executable "python"` — installing python3 fixed that. Now hitting another blocker: can't fetch private images from registry, `docker login` returns 403.
ashley: Registry 403 usually means your service account hasn't been granted the image-pull role. @mira did you set up the GCP SA key or use Workload Identity?
mira: I followed the onboarding doc and tried `gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=~/redwood-sa.json` but the CI tokens page shows no recent activity. Also okta login prompts for MFA but my phone isn't registered yet.
devops-bot: [INFO] Created workspace `mira-dev` in us-central1. Please ensure `gcloud` is configured with `gcloud config set project redwood-dev` and `gcloud auth application-default login` to populate ADC.
sam: Can you paste the exact `docker login` command and the error output? Might be missing `--username _json_key --password-stdin` pattern for GCR.
mira: Error:
```
$ docker login gcr.io
Error response from daemon: Get https://gcr.io/v2/: unauthorized: authentication required
```
I followed the doc which has `cat redwood-sa.json | docker login -u _json_key --password-stdin https://gcr.io`
ashley: That looks right. Two things: (1) confirm the SA JSON is from the project you're trying to pull from, (2) confirm your SA has `roles/storage.objectViewer` and `roles/artifactregistry.reader` depending on registry. I just added you to a temporary group, give it 5–10m to propagate and retry.
jordan: Also note that if you're on VPN split-tunnel, sometimes the corporate IAM endpoints fail. Try disconnecting VPN if you can.
mira: Tried again after 10m, same 403. I can access console UI though. Yanked policy check from the console and SA is missing artifactregistry role.
ashley: Fixed now — added `roles/artifactregistry.reader` to the SA. Confirmed with a test pull from my machine.
mira: Pull succeeded, thank you! Next blocker: kubectl contexts. When I run `kubectl get pods --namespace infra` I get `Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`.
sam: That's usually when the cluster's CA isn't in your kubeconfig or `gcloud container clusters get-credentials` didn't complete. Which cluster name are you targeting?
mira: `redwood-dev-us-central1-a-run1` — ran the gcloud get-credentials but it prints: `Warning: no clusters found`.
jordan: We just spun up a replacement cluster; the name changed to `run1a` — infra pushed a rename. I'll ping infra-ops to add a DNS alias. In meantime, run this to fetch kubeconfig:
```
gcloud container clusters get-credentials run1a --zone us-central1-a --project redwood-dev
```
mira: That worked, kubeconfig updated, pods visible. Thanks.
ashley: Nice. One more small ask: your PR touches the deploy scripts — could you add a quick note in the PR description about why the python3 bump is needed? It helps oncall rollback if something breaks.
mira: Sure, I'll update description.
sam: Review ping — @ashley can you take a quick look at infra/pull/345? There's a tiny CLI tweak and the SA role change request is referenced.
ashley: On it, will try to review before EOD.
mira: Today: finish PR description, submit follow-up doc for registry troubleshooting, finish walkthrough recording for access steps (will share link). Blockers: none remaining for registry/cluster, MFA phone registration scheduled with People Ops.
devops-bot: [REMINDER] New-hire checklist for mira: VPN ✅, Okta MFA pending, SA key configured ✅, registry pull ✅, kube access ✅. If any item remains, open a ticket at https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/CreateIssue.jspa
mira: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:"
